Reference / csv

csv#

In-memory Unicode CSV representations; defaults are comma / double quote / CRLF.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let dialect = CsvDialect(";", "'", "\n");
let rows = CsvRows("name;note\nAda;'one; two'\n", dialect);
let text = CsvString(rows, dialect).string();

Description#

In-memory Unicode CSV representations; defaults are comma / double quote / CRLF.

CsvRows retains source text at construction. Each cursor() validates the WHOLE document before returning independent immutable rows; malformed input cannot expose a partial result. Missing final terminators are accepted. Empty input has zero rows, a terminator alone has one empty field, and a zero-field row cannot be printed. BOM and control scalars are ordinary data. No byte decoding, newline normalization or I/O happens in these objects.

CsvString snapshots a nominal Iterating<@string> exactly once at construction. A row budget rejects after at most maximum_rows+1 item observations, even for an infinite origin. string() checks encoded output size before escaping each record. Repeated calls use the same snapshot and do not revisit origin. No constructor, cursor, printer or destructor closes a borrowed origin.

Defaults: 1048576 input/output scalars, 65536 decoded field scalars, 10000 rows, 1024 columns. Five-argument constructors specify these bounds; six-argument versions append a dialect. All bounds are nonnegative; zero is meaningful. InvalidCsvLimits occurs at construction, CsvLimitExceeded when the corresponding operation observes excess input. InvalidCsv.offset() is a zero-based ORIGINAL Unicode scalar coordinate, including EOF at length().

CsvDialect accepts distinct single-scalar delimiter/quote other than CR/LF, and precisely LF or CRLF. Doubling is the only quote escape. symbol() is the scanner protocol; decoded() undoubles an already validated quoted interior, it is NOT a standalone CSV parser. encoded()/size() handle a single field. record() requires a nonempty field array and counts separators and ending in its allowance. Standalone CsvField/CsvRecord are unbounded default-format representations; bounded documents should use CsvString.

CsvPrefix/Snapshot/PrintPrefix are hidden, immutable implementation collaborators. Prefix parsing retains source spans and decodes each completed field once; applications use CsvRows/CsvString. Each record includes its terminator; an empty document has no records. No header guessing, implicit byte encoding or spreadsheet-specific rewriting.

object CsvRecord#

object CsvRecord

One CSV record: its fields, printed by string(). A record that CsvRecords read also knows its header, so its fields read like json values by column name (#202):

record.text("name");                 // "" for an empty field
record.int("age");                   // MissingCsvValue when empty
record.maybe("note").text() else ""; // an empty field reads as absent

A failure names the row (the header is row 1) and the column.

A record of fields alone, with no header to name them.

object CsvRecords#

object CsvRecords does Iterating<CsvRecord>

The records of a CSV text whose first row names the columns (#202):

for CsvRecords(text) -> record {
    record.text("name");
    record.int("age");
}

A column named twice reads its first field. The text is read and checked whole, as CsvRows reads it.

Records as an AsyncReading gives them, an upload or a socket, are read as they come with for await (#204):

for await CsvRecords(origin: upload) -> record {
    record.text("name");
}

Such a source has the default comma, quote and CRLF grammar and, unless given, the limits of CsvStream: 4 MiB, 1 Mi characters, fields of 64 Ki, 10 000 rows, 1024 columns. Walking it with for, instead of for await, is AsyncCsvOrigin.walked.
